payload.claim: The third witness's claim (test_coverage_problems_names_each_negative_claim_that_declares_no_positive_case) and its accompanying Notes for the agent describe a very large, tightly interlocking fixture: 9 base-word criteria, an upper-case-form criterion, a sentence-initial-form criterion, a dual-word criterion (`not` before `no`, mentioned only in the Notes, not enumerated in the claim's own criterion count), 12 quiet word-inside-a-longer-word criteria (9 explicit plus 3 coined for `neither`/`without`/`cannot`) with only 3 of their positions pinned by the claim ('one quiet claim comes first, one sits among the loud ones, and one comes third from last'), plus two more criteria at the very end carrying the member-line/negation-line ordering and positive_case-suppression behavior. The claim text alone does not pin the full criteria count or every quiet claim's position, relying on the separate, less formal Notes section to fill gaps. I could not find an outright contradiction in this fixture design, but its combinatorial density makes it genuinely easy for an implementing cell to build a fixture that satisfies most but not all of the interlocking constraints while still passing an under-constrained assertion, or to mis-place a required ordering case. A person should sanity-check the third witness's exact fixture text once drafted, before the cell's build is accepted, since the spec's own wording leaves some placement freedom that only the Notes narrow.
